emergency.title: Emergency Help & Travel Tips
emergency.subtitle: Category-based guidance for emergencies foreigners may face in Korea.

passport.title: Passport / Visa & Stay Help
passport.short: When you lose your passport or need visa/stay support

steps.1: If possible, secure a copy/photo of your passport first, then confirm the loss with nearby support (lodging/police).
steps.2: Contact your embassy/consulate for reissue or temporary document procedures.
steps.3: Prepare local police/case number if required.

lost.title: Lost / Theft Report
lost.short: If you lost your wallet, phone, or important belongings

steps.1: If your phone/account may be compromised, stop authentication immediately and change passwords.
steps.2: Report to a nearby police station/lost-and-found center and secure a case number.
steps.3: If passport/cards are also lost, contact your embassy/consulate for urgent action.

safety.title: Crime / Violence / Safety Threat
safety.short: When facing scams, assault, threats, or nearby danger

steps.1: Move to a safe place immediately and ask nearby people/staff for help.
steps.3: Record incident details (time/place) and keep evidence (photos/messages).

medical.title: Emergency Medical / Accident & Injury
medical.short: For sudden illness or injuries from accidents

steps.1: Call 119 or 112 as needed and receive first aid.
steps.2: If interpretation is needed at the hospital, ask embassy/consulate support.
steps.3: Share allergy/medication/chronic condition information with medical staff.

disaster.title: Fire / Disaster & Evacuation
disaster.short: How to respond in fire, heavy rain, blackout, or other disasters

steps.1: Follow alarms/guidance and move to a safe evacuation route.
steps.2: If there are injured people, secure safety first, then request rescue.
steps.3: Share your location and situation with embassy/lodging for help.

immigration.title: Immigration / Deportation & Stay Issues
immigration.short: Administrative issues like overstay or deportation risk

steps.1: Do not respond alone; keep photos of documents/notices and contact your embassy quickly.
steps.2: Request guidance for legal/interpreter support if needed.
steps.3: Avoid unauthorized actions that may affect immigration procedures.

interpreter.title: Consulate / Interpreter Contact Request
interpreter.short: When language barriers make it hard to ask for help

steps.1: Summarize the situation briefly (when/where/what) and share it with your consulate.
steps.2: Prepare a reachable phone number, address, and lodging info.
steps.3: You may need to call emergency lines (police/medical) in parallel.
